function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling “detailed” data about a network interface on the most common operating systems. Pick the section that matches your platform and run the listed commands (or copy‑paste them into a terminal). --- ## 1. Linux | What you want | Command(s) | Notes | |---------------|------------|-------| | **Basic interface state** | `ip link show `
`ip addr show ` | Shows MTU, flags, MAC, IP addresses, and whether it’s up/down. | | **Statistics & counters** | `ethtool -S `
`cat /sys/class/net//statistics/*` | `ethtool -S` gives a nicely formatted view; the sysfs files are raw counters. | | **Driver & firmware** | `ethtool -i `
`modinfo $(basename $(readlink /sys/class/net//device/driver))` | Driver name, firmware version, and module info. | | **Link mode & speed** | `ethtool ` | Displays negotiated speed, duplex, autoneg status, and supported modes. | | **Offload settings** | `ethtool -k ` | Lists enabled/disabled offloads (checksum, TSO, GRO, etc.). | | **Ring buffer sizes** | `ethtool -g ` | Current RX/TX ring buffer lengths. | | **Flow control** | `ethtool -N ` | Flow‑control hash tables. | | **EEPROM contents** | `ethtool -m ` | Raw EEPROM dump (useful for diagnostics). | | **Hardware PCI info** | `lspci -v -s $(cat /sys/class/net//device/physfn/PCI_SLOT_NAME)` | Vendor, device ID, subsystem IDs, class code, revision, driver. | | **Full NIC description** | `lshw -class network -short`
`lshw -class network -numeric` | Hardware tree with vendor, product, serial, bus info. | | **SNMP walk** | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable` | If you have an SNMP agent running locally. | | **Power management** | `ethtool -a ` | Auto‑negotiation of pause frames. | | **LED test** | `ethtool -p ` | Blink LEDs to verify physical connection. | > **Tip:** Replace `` with the actual interface name (`eth0`, `enp3s0`, `ens160`, etc.). --- ## 2. macOS | What you want | Command(s) | Notes | |---------------|------------|-------| | **Interface summary** | `ifconfig ` | Shows flags, MTU, MAC, IP, and link state. | | **Detailed system profiler** | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` | GUI‑style output including vendor, speed, and driver. | | **Network setup info** | `networksetup -getinfo ` | Returns DNS servers, router, and other config. | | **Hardware details** | `ioreg -l -w 0 | grep -A 10 ""` | Low‑level I/O registry dump for the NIC. | | **Statistics** | `netstat -i ` | Packet counters. | | **Driver info** | `kextstat | grep -i ` | Loaded kernel extensions for the NIC. | --- ## 3. Windows (PowerShell) | What you want | Command(s) | Notes | |---------------|------------|-------| | **All adapter properties** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name "" | Format-List *` | Full list of properties (status, MAC, speed, etc.). | | **IP configuration** | `Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias ""` | IPv4/IPv6 addresses, prefixes, gateways. | | **Statistics** | `Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name ""` | Packets sent/received, errors, collisions. | | **Driver details** | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter -Filter "NetConnectionID=''" | Select-Object *` | Driver name, PNPDeviceID, status. | | **Physical NIC info** | `Get-WmiObject Win32_PnPEntity -Filter "PNPDeviceID LIKE '%%'" | Format-List *` | Vendor, device ID, subsystem. | | **NIC performance counters** | `Get-Counter "\Network Adapter()\*"` | Real‑time performance metrics. | > **Tip:** Replace `` with the exact alias shown in `Get-NetAdapter` (e.g., `"Ethernet"` or `"Wi-Fi"`). --- ## 4. Common Cross‑Platform Tools | Tool | What it does | How to use | |------|--------------|------------| | **ethtool** (Linux only) | Interface diagnostics, driver info, statistics, offloads | `ethtool ` | | **iproute2** (`ip`) | Modern replacement for `ifconfig` | `ip ` | | **netstat** | Legacy socket and interface stats | `netstat -i ` | | **ss** | Socket statistics (modern `netstat`) | `ss -i ` | | **SNMP** | Remote monitoring via MIBs | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable` | | **lshw** | Detailed hardware inventory | `sudo lshw -class network` | | **lspci** | PCI bus information | `lspci -v -s ` | | **system_profiler** (macOS) | System inventory report | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` | | **Get-NetAdapter** (Windows PowerShell) | Adapter properties | `Get-NetAdapter -Name ""` | --- ### Quick Checklist 1. **Identify the interface name** (`ip link`, `ifconfig`, `Get-NetAdapter`, `networksetup -listallhardwareports`). 2. **Check operational state** (`ip link show`, `ifconfig`, `Get-NetAdapter`). 3. **Read driver/module info** (`ethtool -i`, `modinfo`, `kextstat`, `Get-WmiObject`). 4. **View statistics** (`ethtool -S`, `cat /sys/.../statistics`, `netstat -i`, `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`). 5. **Inspect hardware identifiers** (PCI slot, vendor/product IDs, serial numbers). Feel free to let me know which OS and interface you’re working with, and I can tailor the commands further!
